alias-ref: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `ref p @ pattern`: K's #as binds the matched term itself; remove `ref`
alias-inside-itself: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: identifier `p` is bound more than once in the same pattern: an alias cannot occur inside its own subpattern (E0416)
alias-remainder: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `p @ ..`: a `..` remainder binds only inside a sequence, collection or cells! pattern
alias-in-result: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `name @ pattern` (K's #as) names the term a pattern matched, so it stands only where a sentence matches: a subject, or a `k::matches!` pattern in a condition; a single-body rule's subject outside its `k::rewrite!` islands is kept as it is, as a context's and a context alias's are around their hole, and a result only builds; here it stands in the result of a `k::rules!` sort rule
alias-whole-subject: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `p @ pattern` cannot alias a whole rule subject: its root is the matched constructor or function; alias a subterm instead
or-unequal-binders: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-or]: variable `x` is not bound in all alternatives
or-ambiguous: error[krs::analysis::ambiguous-or-pattern]: alternatives `Pair(x, y)` and `Pair(y, x)` of this or-pattern can match the same term with different bindings; K's #Or then is ambiguous (LLVM takes one, Haskell explores both). Make them disjoint or split the rule.
or-in-result: error[krs::analysis::ambiguous-operator]: `|` has operands of sorts `Exp` and `Exp`, which choose no builtin domain; write the operation you mean: `a.bit_or::<Int>(b)`; `|` joins pattern alternatives only on a left-hand side
or-remainder: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-or]: or-patterns combine terms, not remainders
or-simplification: error[krs::analysis::invalid-pattern-or]: `A | B` (K's #Or) matches one of several terms, and a subject rewritten as one term in place stands for the one term it matched: write one sentence per alternative; here it stands in the subject of a `#[k::simplification]` fn
matches-shadow: error[krs::analysis::invalid-matches]: `e` in k::matches! binds a new variable; it does not compare with the `e` the sentence or the initializer already names. Use int::eq/bool::eq, or write `_`
matches-guard: error[krs::syntax::invalid-matches]: K's :=K has no guard; conjoin a separate condition with bool::and
matches-std: error[krs::syntax::invalid-matches]: did you mean `k::matches!`? std's matches! tests a host value
matches-lhs: error[krs::expand::matches-outside-condition]: `k::matches!` (K's :=K) computes a Bool by matching a term, the application of a function generated for that test, and no term a pattern meets is an application of it, so a pattern holding one never matches: it stands where a term is built or a condition computed, in a claim's start state, which is a term, and in a key, a set's element or a Set collection's instance that a pattern over evaluated terms computes from names it binds elsewhere and looks up, never where a key selects an entry by matching; write the test in a rule's or an equation's result or condition, a fn body, or an initializer; here it stands in the subject of a `k::rules!` sort rule
matches-alias-result: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `name @ pattern` (K's #as) names the term a pattern matched, so it stands only where a sentence matches: a subject, or a `k::matches!` pattern in a condition; a single-body rule's subject outside its `k::rewrite!` islands is kept as it is, as a context's and a context alias's are around their hole, and a result only builds; here it stands in a `k::matches!` pattern in the result of a `k::rules!` sort rule
matches-sort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-matches]: the pattern has sort `Color` and the subject has sort `Exp`, which share no subsort, so this test is always false
let-shape: error[krs::syntax::invalid-let]: a term block is `let pattern = term;`* followed by one result term (K's #let)
let-or: error[krs::syntax::invalid-let]: a `let` reads its value by one pattern, whose names the rest of its block uses: test which shape a value has with `k::matches!`, or match each shape in a sentence of its own; here it stands in a `let` pattern in the result of an equation
let-alias: error[krs::syntax::invalid-let]: a `let` pattern destructures one value, which a bare name already names whole: write `let p = e; let P = p;` for `p @ P`; here it stands in a `let` pattern in the result of an equation
let-pattern: error[krs::expand::let-outside-term]: a `let` block (K's #let) computes a term, the application `#fun(P => B)(E)` of a function generated for that block, and no term a pattern meets is an application of it, so a pattern holding one never matches: it stands where a term is built or a condition computed, in a claim's start state, which is a term, and in a key, a set's element or a Set collection's instance that a pattern over evaluated terms computes from names it binds elsewhere and looks up, never where a key selects an entry by matching; write the block in a rule's or an equation's result or condition, a fn body, or an initializer; here it stands in the subject of an equation
let-scope: error[krs::expand::unbound-name]: `x` is not bound in this sentence: a bare snake-case name is a binder, and only the pattern (or a `let`, `#[k::exists]`, or `#[k::fresh]`) introduces one; did you mean `e`?
let-sort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-let]: the pattern has sort `Bool` and the value has sort `Exp`, which share no subsort, so this `let` is always undefined
context-remainder: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a function context frames the rest of the configuration with an anonymous `..`
context-bound-rest: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a function context frames the rest of the configuration with an anonymous `..`
context-on-rule: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a configuration context belongs only on #[k::equation] (K's [[ ]] function context)
context-on-simplification: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a configuration context belongs only on #[k::equation] (K's [[ ]] function context)
context-shape: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a function context is a final `k::cells! { cell: .., .. }` parameter typed by the configuration struct or a cell group it holds
context-binders: error[krs::syntax::unsupported-rule-signature]: unsupported rule signature: typed term parameters must declare every term binder of the subject and function context, in first-occurrence order (hole binders included; `_`, remainders, HERE, instance labels and local binders excluded); a sentence with a function context declares every binder, here `n, b`
context-sort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-function-context]: the function-context binder `b` is declared `Bool`, but the cell `bar` holds `Int`
context-group: error[krs::expand::cell-collection-placement]: a context alias and an equation's function context read fixed leaf cells only; the entry of `frame`, which names the whole group cell, is not supported there yet; name the leaf cells inside it, each with an entry of its own
context-overlap: error[krs::analysis::overlapping-rule-heads]: rules `bump` and `read` can both apply to the same configuration at the same priority; K would take either one (nondeterminism). If that is intended, put both in one group with `#[k::rule(nondet = NAME)]`; otherwise refine a pattern, add disjoint `where` sorts or complementary requires guards, or order them with `owise` or `priority = N`.

Make the equations disjoint (a pattern, or a `requires` that excludes the argument), or give one of them another priority (`owise` or `priority = N`).

Make the equations disjoint (a pattern, or a `requires` that excludes the argument), or give one of them another priority (`owise` or `priority = N`).
